selected_news.source_headline: Beware ‘sun, sea and surgery’ cosmetic tourism packages, experts advise
selected_news.article_text: British College of Aesthetic Medicine launches checklist as part of ‘vet it before you get it’ campaign Cosmetic tourism is often sold as a package of sun, sea and surgery, but experts have said travelling overseas for procedures can end in infections, disfigurement and death Nora Nugent, a consultant plastic surgeon and former president of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons, said travelling to countries such as Turkey for surgery came with myriad risks – and not just on the operating table “Actually, the risks start from the moment you step on the plane to after you return home, and until you’re fully healed and you’re out of the clotting risk time,” she said, noting that travel itself could increase the risks of clots. A lack of in-person aftercare is also a concern The British College of Aesthetic Medicine has launched a checklist as part of its “vet it before you get it” campaign, intended to help potential patients make better and safer choices about overseas cosmetic surgery As well as setting out red flags to look out for, the campaign suggests those seeking cosmetic surgery independently verify a surgeon’s qualifications, determine what emergency facilities are available near the chosen clinic and find out what insurance the practitioner has in place Nugent said a major driver for patients seeking procedures in countries such as Turkey was their relative cheapness, but that prices were high in the UK as a result of factors including the higher cost of living and higher fees for medical indemnity and insurance Chrissie Wolfe, the founder and chief executive of Lupa Law, a specialist medical negligence practice, said there could be a host of difficulties in making a claim should a procedure go wrong overseas, and that even if compensation were awarded, it could be far lower than in the UK “Turkey is the most popular destination by far for cosmetic surgery, but it is absolutely the most difficult from a legal perspective,” she said. “When something goes wrong, it’s incredibly difficult to put right.” She said those looking to undergo cosmetic surgery abroad should be wary of clinics selling bundles of procedures or time-limited deals, noting that one patient had gone to Turkey for a tummy tuck but was upsold a “mummy makeover” that included a breast uplift “She came back and had a very severe infection,” she said. “She ultimately ended up losing most of her left breast and the entire right breast on a procedure that she didn’t even want in the first place.” Wolfe said the marketing of travelling abroad for cosmetic surgery as a glossy holiday was problematic. “It shifts the patient’s mind away from the seriousness of what they’re actually embarking on,” she said It is not the first time overseas cosmetic surgery has sparked warnings. The then health secretary, Wes Streeting, urged caution over such procedures in 2024 Data, however, suggests growing numbers of residents in Great Britain are travelling overseas for medical treatment. According to data from the Office for National Statistics, about 524,000 did so in 2024, including cosmetic procedures, up from 431,000 in 2023 Brazillian butt lifts (BBLs) have the highest risk of death, but other overseas procedures have also left patients with problems Nugent cited the case of a woman who had developed abscesses and infections in her neck after a facelift. She needed long-term antibiotics and drainage procedures and was left with significant scarring Another woman in her late 20s had a breast lift and labiaplasty abroad after pregnancy. She ended up with a loss of tissue on one breast, her implant exposed and over-reduced labia. As a result she needed corrective surgeries, including to redo the lifts and improve the labiaplasty “But you can’t get things back to how they were,” said Nugent A third woman underwent a tummy tuck overseas, she said, but the wound came apart and required surgical cleaning. She has been left with scarring and a dip in her tummy “These are three examples of patients who suffered fairly horrific complications from procedures that were meant to improve how they looked and how they felt about themselves and have ended up doing exactly the opposite,” Nugent said

selected_news.title: Afyon’da 8 ölü, 1 yaralı; Eskişehir’de tutuklandı
selected_news.summary: Victims are found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports.
selected_news.source_headline: Eight killed in series of shootings in western Turkey
selected_news.article_text: Eight people have been killed and one seriously injured in a series of shootings in western Turkey The attacks took place in the Afyonkarahisar province on Thursday, with victims found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports The suspect fled, triggering a manhunt, and authorities later said he had been arrested in Eskişehir province CCTV footage published in Turkish media showed a man in a black jacket, white trousers and glasses clutching a long weapon as he stood by a red minivan Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency reported that three people were killed near Ayazini village and three others near Kiyir village. In Yukaritandir, two women were found injured and later died in hospital Two teachers were reportedly among the dead Local media said roads leading to the affected villages were closed by police, while officers launched a large-scale operation to find the suspect The newspaper Milliyet reported that a vehicle allegedly taken by the attacker had been later found stuck in mud - the suspect having abandoned it before fleeing on foot In a statement posted on social media, the Afyonkarahisar Governorate said "all relevant institutions of our state have been working in coordination since the very first moment and are meticulously carrying out the necessary work"

selected_news.title: Russell Brand’a iki yeni tecavüz iddiası soruşturuluyor
selected_news.summary: Detective urges other potential victims to come forward and says: ‘Our work’s not done’ The lead detective in the case against Russell Brand has urged other potential victims of the comedian to come forward after it emerged he is under investigation for two further rape allegations and faces a civil claim in the UK. Det Supt Andy Furphy, the Metropolitan police’s strategic lead in the investigation, described Brand, 51, as “a predator” whose behaviour escalated as his fame grew. Continue reading...
selected_news.source_headline: Police investigating two further rape allegations against Russell Brand
selected_news.article_text: Detective urges other potential victims to come forward and says: ‘Our work’s not done’ The lead detective in the case against Russell Brand has urged other potential victims of the comedian to come forward after it emerged he is under investigation for two further rape allegations and faces a civil claim in the UK Det Supt Andy Furphy, the Metropolitan police’s strategic lead in the investigation, described Brand, 51, as “a predator” whose behaviour escalated as his fame grew On Thursday, Brand was found guilty of raping a fan and sexually assaulting three women over five years at the height of his career. He was cleared of two further counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault after a four-week trial at Southwark crown court It can now be revealed that Brand is under investigation for two further rape allegations and that the Met has submitted files to the Crown Prosecution Service Brand has also been accused of sexually assaulting a woman at his mansion in Los Angeles in 2008, in a civil claim filed at the high court in London The Met’s investigation into Brand, named Operation Actinolite, involved tracing and speaking to more than 100 witnesses, reviewing more than 1,400 documents and taking more than 340 statements, including from Brand’s former employers, colleagues and associates Speaking after Brand’s conviction, Furphy said the police investigation was continuing and he believed there could be more victims “If you get a conviction then it tends to encourage other people to come forward because they see the courage and the bravery and the resilience that these women have had to go through this criminal justice process, and they feel their own strength as a result of that. They want to come forward and have their story told,” he told the Guardian “So, yes, there may be more victims of Russell Brand out there, but for now our focus remains on the women that came forward.” The Met said Brand had been interviewed under caution in connection with two further rape allegations made by two women. “Files have been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in relation to both complainants. Detectives remain in close contact with prosecutors as inquiries continue and further investigative work is carried out,” a spokesperson said Pre-trial legal documents suggested there were outstanding charges against Brand in relation to a woman who made allegations about him in a Channel 4 Dispatches documentary in 2023. She accused Brand of grooming her and sending a BBC car to bring her to him from the gates of her school when she was a 16-year-old pupil Furphy refused to comment on any outstanding inquiries but appealed for women to come forward if they had anything to report “We have a live investigation. Our work’s not done,” Furphy said. “What I would say, is if you’ve been affected by the case, if Russell Brand has committed a crime against you, rape or serious sexual violence or a sex assault, whatever it might be, and you haven’t spoken to police yet, then come forward. We’ve got specially trained staff, specially trained officers. We’ll support you and listen to you.” It is understood a couple of other women made allegations against Brand during the Met’s investigation but they did not result in charges Furphy said Brand had abused his celebrity status to assault women who then feared they would not be believed “Russell Brand is a predator,” Furphy said. “He preys on women and commits serious sexual offences against them. He’s in a position of power, a celebrity, he’s wealthy “If you look at the offending from the first date up until when the final offences were committed, you can see an escalation in his behaviour. The more famous he gets, the more emboldened he gets, less likely to be challenged, less likely to be held accountable. He’s been held accountable now.” He praised the “really courageous, brave and resilient women” who gave evidence against him while facing the intense scrutiny of Brand’s barrister, Ian Winter KC. He described the cross-examination as “deeply uncomfortable” “Rape and serious sexual offences is a deeply personal thing, people are recounting some of the worst things that have ever happened to them,” he said. “We can perceive that line of questioning may come, but I’ve got to be honest with you, it was deeply uncomfortable at times.” Brand gave interviews to Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly and Piers Morgan before the trial and continued podcasting throughout, which the detective said had taken a toll on the women “It’d be fair to say that what he did to them has had a very long-lasting effect on them, in the way they trust people … it’s been devastating to many of them,” Furphy said “Then a challenging aspect of this [case] was the constant public commentary around it, and some of that was coming from him. And as you can imagine in a case like this, as an investigation team, we’ve got to review everything – DVDs, books, podcasts, stuff that’s appearing online “So, for me, he drove right up to the line of what was acceptable in a live criminal trial and stopped just short. But that doesn’t mean we weren’t prepared to take action if it started to cross over that line, and the women who’ve put their trust in us knew that.” Furphy said the case may be a “watershed moment” in inspiring a wave of other victims of sexual offences to come forward. “I think if you look back to that culture during that period of time, that kind of lad culture, there may be other victims that come forward regarding other people.” Brand is already facing civil claims in Britain and the US. In court papers seen by the Guardian, a woman who has begun civil proceedings in London has claimed Brand forcibly removed her dress, shoes and underwear, pushed her on to his bed and attempted “to perform oral sex on her against her will” She said she eventually managed to break free from his grasp but was left “terrified and shaking violently” as she ran from the house. She said she later suffered from PTSD symptoms. Brand denies her claims, which he described via his lawyers as “fundamentally dishonest” The case was lodged last year but was stayed until the proceedings in the criminal case against Brand concluded this week. A claim form filed in February 2025 suggests the woman is seeking damages of up to £100,000 The woman said she felt “traumatised by the rage Brand displayed when she refused to submit to him sexually” and feared her safety would be at risk if she pursued a criminal complaint However, she decided to report her allegation to the Met in 2025. She said she was “fortified” by other women who had come forward to make allegations against Brand The woman’s case was not included in the trial. The Guardian understands this was largely because the offence was alleged to have occurred in the US, meaning the English criminal courts did not have jurisdiction to prosecute A separate civil claim was filed in the US in 2023 over allegations Brand sexually assaulted a woman in 2010 while filming the movie Arthur None of the victims in the criminal case have submitted compensation claims
